label: Filter name
summary: The name of a message filter, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a label in the message settings window. Going by its name and that use, it is the shown name of one filter entry.

label: Filter tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a message filter, as text.
details: Vanilla puts it into the tooltip of an entry in the message settings window. Going by its name and that use, it explains the filter when the mouse rests on it.

label: Filter options
summary: The list of options that can be chosen for a message filter.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of a selection box in the message settings window. The game does not name the type of the list items.

label: Has auto-pause
summary: Whether the message filter is set to pause the game automatically.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a checkbox in the message settings window. Going by its name and that use, a checked box means the game pauses when such a message arrives.

label: Select filter option
summary: Runs when another option is picked for a message filter.
details: Vanilla calls it from the selection-changed event of a selection box in the message settings window. It returns nothing; it only acts.

label: Filter itself
summary: The message filter item itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Toggle auto-pause
summary: Switches the automatic pause of a message filter on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the message settings window, next to the checkbox that shows the auto-pause state. It returns nothing.

label: Filter type itself
summary: Access to the message filter type object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Filter type itself
summary: The message filter type itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Message group itself
summary: Access to the message group item object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Group filters
summary: The list of message filters that belong to a message group.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of a list widget in the message settings window, so each group shows its own filters. The game does not name the list item type, but the filter items of this window are the likely ones.

label: Group title
summary: The title of a message group, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a heading in the message settings window. Going by its name and that use, it is the shown name of the group.

label: Group type
summary: The message group type of a message group.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the message settings window, so that part can use the functions of the group type. The game does not name the return type.

label: Message group itself
summary: The message group item itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Group type itself
summary: Access to the message group type object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Group type name
summary: The name of a message group type, as text.
details: The input has no line using it on this type. Other types have a function of the same name that returns their shown name, so this one is likely the shown name of the group type. That is a hint from the name only.

label: Group type itself
summary: The message group type itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Log entry itself
summary: Access to the message log entry object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Log entry message
summary: The message that a message log entry holds.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the message settings window, so that part can show the message with its own functions. The game does not name the return type.

label: Mark log entry for deletion
summary: Marks a message log entry to be deleted.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the message settings window. Going by its name, the entry is only marked; when it is actually removed is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Log entry itself
summary: The message log entry itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Popup itself
summary: Access to the message popup object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Close popup
summary: Closes the message popup window.
details: Vanilla calls it from two click events in the message popup window. It returns nothing.

label: Popup message
summary: The message that the popup shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the message popup window, so that part can show the message with its own functions. The game does not name the return type.

label: Popup itself
summary: The message popup itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Settings window itself
summary: Access to the message settings window object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Close with confirmation
summary: Closes the message settings window, asking for confirmation first.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the message settings window. Going by its name, a confirmation is asked before the window closes; what is confirmed and when is not documented. It returns nothing.

label: Custom message window
summary: The window object for the custom message settings.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as the data context of a part of the message settings window. The game does not name the return type.

label: Filtered message filters
summary: The list of message filters that match the current text filter.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of a list in the message settings window. Going by its name, it is the filter list after the search text is applied; the game does not name the item type.

label: Message groups
summary: The list of message groups shown in the message settings window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list that builds the group sections of the window. The game does not name the item type, but it is the message group item type of this window.

label: Message log entries
summary: The list of message log entries shown in the message settings window.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as a data list in the window. Going by its name, these are the past messages, the log history. The game does not name the item type.

label: Search text
summary: The text typed into the search field of the message settings window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of the search field. Going by its name and that use, it is the text used to narrow the list of filters.

label: Search text is empty
summary: Whether the search field of the message settings window is empty.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of widgets, once as is and once negated with Not, so some parts show only with an empty search and others only with some text.

label: Search text edited
summary: Runs when the search text of the message settings window is edited.
details: Vanilla calls it from the text-edited event of the search field. Going by its name, it makes the window re-apply the search. It returns nothing.

label: Reset to default
summary: Resets the message settings to their default values.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the message settings window. It returns nothing. Going by its name, the player's changed settings are replaced by the defaults.

label: Save and close
summary: Saves the message settings and closes the window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the message settings window. It returns nothing.

label: Settings window itself
summary: The message settings window itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Message type itself
summary: Access to the message type object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Message type icon
summary: The icon of a message type.
details: The input has no line using it on this type. Other types have a function of the same name that supplies a texture, so this one likely gives the icon picture. That is a hint from the name only; the game does not name the return type.

label: Has flag
summary: Whether the message type carries the given flag.
details: The input has no line using it on this type. Other types use a function of the same name with a quoted flag name, for example a law group checked for 'realm_no_pass'. Going by that, the argument is a flag name in quotes. Which flags a message type has is not documented here.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The flag name to look for.
fields.values: a quoted text, such as 'dangerous' (the example is from another type)

label: Has any flags
summary: Whether the message type has any flags at all.
details: Vanilla (in the notification templates) calls it on the type of a player message, negated with Not, to decide whether a part is shown. Going by its name, it is true when at least one flag is set.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the message type has an icon.
details: The input has no line using it on this type. Other types have a function of the same name that is used for the visibility of an icon widget, so this one likely tells whether there is an icon to show. That is a hint from the name only.

label: Is bad message
summary: Whether the message type counts as bad news.
details: Vanilla (in the notification templates) uses it on the type of a player message to show a widget for bad messages. It sits beside IsGood and IsNeutral, which show the other looks.

label: Is good message
summary: Whether the message type counts as good news.
details: Vanilla (in the notification templates) uses it on the type of a player message to show a widget for good messages. It sits beside IsBad and IsNeutral, which show the other looks.

label: Is neutral message
summary: Whether the message type counts as neither good nor bad news.
details: Vanilla (in the notification templates) uses it on the type of a player message to show a widget for neutral messages. It sits beside IsGood and IsBad, which show the other looks.

label: Is no message type
summary: Whether the message type is the empty 'none' type.
details: Vanilla (in the message settings window) combines it with IsNeutral using Or, so a widget is shown for neutral messages and for those without a type. Going by its name, it is true when no real type is set.

label: Message type itself
summary: The message type itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Meta info widget itself
summary: Access to the meta info widget object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Meta info widget itself
summary: The meta info widget itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Migration icon itself
summary: Access to the migration map icon object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Domain fertility
summary: The fertility number of the domain that a migration map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla shows it as text on the map icon, rounded to a whole number with the |0 format. Going by its name, it is the fertility figure of the icon's domain.

label: Icon title
summary: The title that a migration map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the map icon, so that part can use the functions of a title. The game does not name the return type.

label: Icon tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a migration map icon, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the icon on the map, twice.

label: Average fertility in range
summary: Whether the average fertility of the icon's area lies between two numbers.
details: Vanilla calls it with number literals written as '(CFixedPoint)0.3' to show a different look for each band: 0.0 to 0.3, 0.3 to 0.6 and 0.6 to 1.1. Whether the end points count as inside is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The lower end of the range.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The upper end of the range.

label: Is domain icon
summary: Whether the migration map icon stands for a domain.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of parts of the icon, alone and combined with IsSelected using And and Not, so a domain icon looks different when it is selected.

label: Is selected icon
summary: Whether the migration map icon is the selected one.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of parts of the icon, alone, negated, and combined with IsDomain, so a selected icon looks different.

label: Migration icon itself
summary: The migration map icon itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set migration target
summary: Makes the icon's area the target of the migration.
details: Vanilla calls it from clicks on the map icon, three times. Going by its name and the window it belongs to, this chooses where the migration goes. It returns nothing.

label: Migration window itself
summary: Access to the migration window object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Clear migration target
summary: Removes the chosen migration target.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the migration window. It returns nothing.

label: Close migration window
summary: Closes the migration window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the migration window. It returns nothing.

label: Close involved rulers list
summary: Closes the list of characters involved in the migration.
details: Vanilla calls it from two clicks in the migration window. It returns nothing.

label: Average fertility
summary: The average fertility of the migration window's area, as a number.
details: The input has no line using it on this type. A vanilla text uses a function of the same name on a title to show that title's average fertility, so this is likely the same idea for the window. That is a hint from the name only.

label: Interaction confirmation window
summary: The confirmation window object for the character interaction that sends the migration.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the migration window. The enabled state of the send button also asks the confirmation window's CanSend. The game does not name the return type.

label: Combined military strength
summary: The combined military strength shown in the migration window, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a text of the migration window, after a soldier icon and the label for combined military strength. Whose strength is added up is not documented.

label: Custom migration effects
summary: The list of custom effects of the migration.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the migration window. Going by its name, these are custom effects of the migration. The game does not name the return type.

label: De jure fertility tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the fertility of the de jure area.
details: The input shows no use anywhere. Going by its name, it is the tooltip about fertility of the de jure (legal) territory. The game documents nothing more.

label: Domain title
summary: The title of the domain shown in the migration window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the migration window, so that part can use the functions of a title. The game does not name the return type.

label: Fertility progress
summary: A fertility progress value, as a number.
details: The input shows no use anywhere. Going by its name, it is a progress value about fertility. The game documents nothing more.

label: Involved characters
summary: The list of characters involved in the migration.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a list in the migration window. A text there also reads GetTotalNumber of this list to show a count on the 'View all Rulers' button. The game does not name the return type.

label: Migration situation
summary: The situation object that the migration window belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the migration window, so that part can use the functions of a situation. The game does not name the return type.

label: Target fertility bar
summary: The fertility bar object for the target domain.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the migration window. Going by its name, it feeds a bar that shows the fertility of the chosen target. The game does not name the return type.

label: Target fertility tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the fertility of the target domain, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of parts of the migration window, twice.

label: Target title
summary: The title that the migration is aimed at.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of parts of the migration window. It also checks IsValid on it, together with the confirmation window's CanSend, to enable the send button. So the button works only when a valid target title is chosen.

label: Title tier
summary: The title tier the migration window currently shows, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it with the |U format in a text and compares it to 'county' with EqualTo_string to set a button's pressed state. Other values seen in vanilla for the setter are 'duchy' and 'kingdom'.

label: Top character
summary: The top character shown in the migration window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the migration window, so that part can use the functions of a character. Which character counts as the top one is not documented.

label: Total herd
summary: The total herd size, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in a text labelled 'Total Herd Size' with a herd icon in the migration window.

label: Has target
summary: Whether a migration target has been chosen.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of a part of the migration window.

label: Has valid selection
summary: Whether the current selection in the migration window is valid.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of parts of the window, once alone and once together with Character.IsValid using And.

label: Target fertility in range
summary: Whether the average fertility of the target domain lies between two numbers.
details: Vanilla calls it with number literals written as '(CFixedPoint)0.3' to show a different look for each band: 0.0 to 0.001, 0.3 to 0.6 and 0.6 to 1.1. Whether the end points count as inside is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The lower end of the range.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The upper end of the range.

label: Involved list is open
summary: Whether the list of involved characters is open.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of a part of the migration window.

label: Shows realm
summary: Whether the migration window shows realms (realm colors).
details: Vanilla uses it for visibility, negated with Not for the opposite look, and for the pressed state of a button. It goes with ToggleRealmColor, which switches it. Going by its name, it picks realm display over the other display.

label: Send migration
summary: Runs when the player sends the migration.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the migration window. It returns nothing.

label: Open involved rulers list
summary: Opens the list of characters involved in the migration.
details: The input shows no use in the game files; vanilla uses ToggleInvolvedCharacterListWindow instead. It returns nothing.

label: Refresh effects
summary: Reloads the migration effects shown in the window.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the migration window. Going by its name, it recalculates the list of effects. It returns nothing.

label: Migration window itself
summary: The migration window itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set title tier
summary: Changes the title tier that the migration window shows.
details: Vanilla calls it from clicks on tier buttons with 'county', 'duchy' or 'kingdom'. The current tier can be read back with GetTitleTier. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle involved rulers list
summary: Opens the list of involved characters if it is closed, and closes it if it is open.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click in the migration window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle realm color
summary: Switches the realm color display of the migration window on or off.
details: Vanilla calls it from two clicks in the migration window. It goes with IsShowRealm, which tells the current state. It returns nothing.

label: Military item itself
summary: Access to the military item object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can create a men-at-arms type
summary: Whether at least one men-at-arms type can be created.
details: Vanilla uses it twice for the visibility of parts of the military window. Going by its name, men-at-arms types are the kinds of regiment that can be created.

label: Can recruit from subjects
summary: Whether troops can be recruited from the subjects.
details: The input shows no use anywhere. Going by its name, it checks the option to recruit from subjects. The game documents nothing more.

label: Item composition
summary: The composition of the military item, meaning what kinds of troops it holds.
details: The input has no line using it on this type. Other types have a function of the same name used as a data context for a composition display. That is a hint from the name only; the game does not name the return type.

label: Controlled men-at-arms
summary: The men-at-arms regiments that the item controls.
details: The input shows no use anywhere. Going by its name, it is a list of men-at-arms under its control. The game documents nothing more.

label: Men-at-arms count and cap
summary: The number of men-at-arms and their limit, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of a label in the military window. Going by its name, it reads like 'count / cap'.

label: Men-at-arms count tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the men-at-arms count and limit, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the military window, next to the count label.

label: Men-at-arms text
summary: A men-at-arms text, as text.
details: The input shows no use anywhere. Going by its name, it is a text about men-at-arms. The game documents nothing more.

label: Men-at-arms tooltip
summary: A men-at-arms tooltip text, as text.
details: The input shows no use anywhere. Going by its name, it is a tooltip about men-at-arms. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can create men-at-arms tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that tells whether a new men-at-arms regiment can be created, as text.
details: Vanilla adds it to the tooltip of the 'Create New men-at-arms regiment' button, under a heading, so it likely gives the reason or the condition.

label: Owned men-at-arms
summary: The list of men-at-arms regiments that the item owns.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data list of the owned regiments in the military window, and checks it with IsDataModelEmpty to show or hide a part. The game does not name the item type.

label: Recruit from subjects tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the recruit-from-subjects button, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the military window.

label: Item title
summary: The title that the military item belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the military window, so that part can use the functions of a title. The game does not name the return type.

label: Upgrade horde tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about upgrading the horde, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the military window. Going by its name, it concerns upgrading a horde.

label: Nomad view is open
summary: Whether the nomad part of the military item is open.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button in the military window. Going by their names, OnClickNomad opens or closes that part.

label: Is open
summary: Whether the military item is expanded in the list.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as the pressed state of buttons in the military window. Going by its name and that use, it is true when the item's section is open.

label: Recruit-from-subjects view is open
summary: Whether the recruit-from-subjects part of the item is open.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of a button in the military window. Going by their names, OnClickSubjects opens or closes that part.

label: Men-at-arms can be created
summary: Whether a men-at-arms regiment can be created now.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of parts of the military window, alone and negated with Not, so a create button and a hint for the opposite case are shown in turn.

label: Click item
summary: Runs when the military item is clicked.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click event in the military window. Going by its name, it opens or closes the item. It returns nothing.

label: Click nomad part
summary: Runs when the nomad part of the military item is clicked.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click event in the military window. Going by its name, it belongs with IsNomadViewOpen. It returns nothing.

label: Click subjects part
summary: Runs when the recruit-from-subjects part of the item is clicked.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click event in the military window. Going by its name, it belongs with IsRecruitFromSubjectsViewOpen. It returns nothing.

label: Click title
summary: Runs when a title of the military item is clicked.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click event and passes the clicked title with Title.Self. It returns nothing; what it does with the title is not documented.

label: Military item itself
summary: The military item itself, so it can be passed to another function.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and by lines of other types that pass .Self as an argument, it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Should show item
summary: Whether the military item should be shown in the list.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of the item in the military window.

label: Show recruit-from-subjects button
summary: Whether the recruit-from-subjects button should be shown.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of a button in the military window.

label: All administrative armies
summary: The list of all armies of administrative titles, for use as a data list.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as the data list in the military window. The game does not name the item type. GetAllAdministrativeArmies is a similar function that vanilla does not use.

label: Military view itself
summary: Access to the military view object itself.
details: The input shows no use for this type. Going by its name and the use of AccessSelf on other types (passed as an argument to another function), it hands the object on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Army automation options shown
summary: Whether the army automation options are shown.
details: The input shows no use anywhere. Going by its name, it tells if the automation options of armies are visible. The game documents nothing more.

label: Knights are shown
summary: Whether the list of knights is shown in the military view.
details: Vanilla uses it for the visibility of the knight list, and in a tooltip text to say 'hide the list' or 'show a list' of the player's knights.

label: Levies are shown
summary: Whether the levy details are shown in the military view.
details: Vanilla uses it twice for visibility, and in a tooltip text to say 'hide' or 'show' the details for the player's levies.

label: Can add rally point
summary: Whether a rally point can be added now.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as the enabled state of a button in the military window. GetAddRallyPointTooltip is used as the tooltip of such a button, which may explain the state.

label: Can request any title army
summary: Whether the player can personally request the army of at least one title.
details: Vanilla combines it with Not(GetPlayer.IsIndependentRuler) using And for the visibility of a part of the military window, so it shows only for rulers who are not independent.

label: Can request title army
summary: Whether the player can personally request the army of the given title.
details: Vanilla passes the title with Title.Self and combines the result with other checks (such as IsAdminTitleWithTroops and a check for hired troops) for visibility in the military window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The title whose army would be requested.

label: Can return controlled men-at-arms
summary: Whether controlled men-at-arms can be returned.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of a button, and in a tooltip text it adds a 'no troops' note when it is false.

label: Can return reassigned men-at-arms
summary: Whether reassigned men-at-arms can be returned.
details: Vanilla uses it as the enabled state of a button, and in a tooltip text it adds a 'no troops' note when it is false.

label: Can use any holy order
summary: Whether at least one holy order can be used.
details: Vanilla combines its negation with DataModelHasItems on the list of all holy orders, so a part is shown when holy orders exist but none can be used.

label: Close military view
summary: Closes the military window.
details: Vanilla calls it from two clicks in the military window. It returns nothing.

label: Other uncontrolled titles exist
summary: Whether other titles exist that the player does not control.
details: Vanilla uses it negated with Not for the visibility of a part of the military window. Going by its name, it is about titles that the player does not control.

label: Add rally point tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the add-rally-point button, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as a tooltip in the military window. It goes with CanAddRallyPoint.

label: All administrative armies
summary: The list of all armies of administrative titles.
details: The input shows no use of this function; vanilla uses AccessAllAdministrativeArmies instead. The game does not name the item type.

label: Hireable rulers
summary: The list of rulers that can be hired, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data list in the military window and checks it with IsDataModelEmpty to show a list or an empty hint. The game does not name the item type.

label: All holy orders
summary: The list of all holy orders.
details: Vanilla counts it with GetDataModelSize for a number, and uses DataModelHasItems on it to fade a widget (alpha 1.0 with items, 0.5 without). The game does not name the item type.

label: All mercenaries
summary: The list of all mercenary companies.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data list in the military window. The game does not name the item type.

label: Barter goods expenses when all raised
summary: The military expenses paid in barter goods if all forces were raised.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the military window. Going by its name, it is the barter goods share of the cost of having everything raised. The game does not name the return type.

label: Gold balance when all raised
summary: The gold balance if all forces were raised, as a number.
details: The input shows no use anywhere. Going by its name, it is the gold balance with everything raised. The game documents nothing more.

label: Gold expenses when all raised
summary: The military expenses paid in gold if all forces were raised.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as the data context of parts of the military window. Going by its name, it is the gold share of the cost of having everything raised. The game does not name the return type.

label: Piety expenses when all raised
summary: The military expenses paid in piety if all forces were raised.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as the data context of parts of the military window. Going by its name, it is the piety share of the cost of having everything raised. The game does not name the return type.

label: Prestige expenses when all raised
summary: The military expenses paid in prestige if all forces were raised.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as the data context of parts of the military window. Going by its name, it is the prestige share of the cost of having everything raised. The game does not name the return type.

label: Time all raised, gold
summary: How long the player's gold lasts with all forces raised, as text.
details: Vanilla puts it into the 'Maximum Military Maintenance' tooltip: with the current gold and income, all troops can stay raised for this long before bankruptcy. It is also shown in brackets as a short label in the military window.

label: Time all raised, treasury
summary: A time figure about keeping all forces raised, for the treasury, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets in a text of the military window, beside the matching gold figure (GetAllRaisedTimeGold, a time before bankruptcy). Going by its name and that neighbour, it is the treasury counterpart.

label: Treasury expenses when all raised
summary: The military expenses paid from the treasury if all forces were raised.
details: Vanilla uses it twice as the data context of parts of the military window. Going by its name, it is the treasury share of the cost of having everything raised. The game does not name the return type.

label: Barter goods expenses
summary: The current military expenses paid in barter goods.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the military window, and also checks the gold and treasury expenses against zero in the same condition, so a part shows only when nothing is spent. The game does not name the return type.

label: Raise event troops tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about raising event troops, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the military window. Going by its name, it explains whether event troops can be raised.

label: Character
summary: The character that the military view is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of parts of the knights window, and passes its GetID when opening the create-accolade view. The game does not name the return type; the uses are those of a character.

label: Army composition
summary: The composition of the military view's forces, meaning what kinds of troops there are.
details: Vanilla uses it three times as the data context of parts of the military window. The game does not name the return type.

label: Default raid intent
summary: The default raid intent offered in the military view.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the military window. Going by its name, a raid intent is the goal chosen for a raid. The game does not name the return type.

label: Divergence breakdown
summary: The breakdown of the divergence for the given holy order rite.
details: Vanilla passes HolyOrder.GetRite.Self and uses the result as the data context of a part of the military window. What exactly divergence is here is not documented. The game does not name the return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The rite whose divergence is broken down.

label: Event troops
summary: The list of troops that came from events.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data list in the military window and hides a part when the list is empty. Going by its name, these are troops that come from events. The game does not name the item type.

label: Gold expenses
summary: The current military expenses paid in gold.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context twice, and also compares its fixed-point value with zero, in a condition that also checks the other kinds of expenses. The game does not name the return type.

label: Held title items
summary: The list of held title entries in the military view.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data list in the military window and checks it with DataModelHasItems for visibility. The game does not name the item type.

label: Hired holy orders
summary: The list of holy orders that the player has hired.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data list in the military window. Together with the hired mercenaries it decides, using Or, whether a part is shown. The game does not name the item type.
